name: review-decision
title: Review decision
purpose: The end of a task: what the checks found and what the review said, one line each, then Accept and Reject, and the result once decided.
whenToUse: Once, at the end of a task's screen, when the work waits for the reader to accept or reject it.
With the checks' line and the review's line even when one has nothing to report: say that no checks are set up, or why there is no review.
Kept in place after the decision, with the result in place of the buttons.
whenNotToUse: For an agent's request to run a tool or a command. Use the approval.
For the full results of the checks or the full review. Show them above it with the check list and a disclosure, and keep this to one line each.
On a row of a list of tasks. Put plain Accept and Reject buttons in the row, never primary, and the decision on the task's own screen.
To ask before something is lost. Reject opens a confirm dialog that asks what becomes of the branch.
accessibility: Use a section with aria-labelledby pointing at ds-review-decision__title, a heading such as Your decision. Its level is the one under the heading it sits beneath. The examples use h4 only because of where they sit on the gallery page.

ds-review-decision__evidence is a dl. Each ds-review-decision__line holds a dt, ds-review-decision__source, naming where the finding comes from (Checks, Review), and a dd, ds-review-decision__finding, saying it in one sentence.

The checks' finding opens with a badge from the status set, with its icon: Checks passed or Checks failed in the tone and icon of Check passed and Check failed. With no checks set up, write that, with no badge, so nothing reads as a pass.

The review's finding is the reviewer and its verdict in words, with no badge, tone or icon, followed by ds-review-decision__caveat saying it is a model's opinion, not a check. A review is never drawn as a check, and never counted with them.

ds-review-decision__actions holds Accept first, as the view's one primary action, and Reject, a plain button, at the far end. Both carry data-ds-critical and are never inside a details element. When the task's checks left files that accepting removes, Accept opens a confirm dialog naming them. Reject always opens a confirm dialog that asks whether to keep or delete the branch and says that nothing is merged or pushed.
An optional note is a field before the actions, labelled Note (optional), sent with whichever button is pressed. It is always in view, so pressing Reject moves no focus to it.

While the decision is sent, set aria-busy="true" on the pressed button, change its label to Accepting or Rejecting, and disable the other. If sending fails, restore both and put an alert with role="alert" before the actions, saying what was not done.

Once decided, replace ds-review-decision__actions and the note with ds-review-decision__result: a badge, Accepted or Rejected with the status set's icon and tone, then a sentence saying what became of the branch and whether anything was merged or pushed. A copy field for the merge command may follow. The pressed button goes with the actions, so move focus to the section's heading, given tabindex="-1", and never let it drop to the page.
The component needs no script. The app sets aria-busy and disabled and swaps the actions for the result.
